🧳 External / portable drive · 🔐 Encrypted or locked

Recover Data From an Encrypted External Drive

Many external drives encrypt data, either with software like BitLocker or Mac's built-in drive encryption, or with hardware encryption, as on many WD My Passport and My Book drives. Without the password or recovery key, recovery is not realistic.

3/5 · Take care
Success odds: Varies

Unlocking with a known key is low risk, but taking a hardware-encrypted drive out of its enclosure can make the data unreadable.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Do not remove the drive from its enclosure if it uses hardware encryption. The key may be tied to the bridge board, and a different adapter can show unreadable data.
  • Do not format or reset it. That destroys the key and the data.
  • Do not trust tools or people claiming to crack or brute-force strong encryption.

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If the drive or its board is damaged and you hold the password or key, a professional may be able to help; without the key, no one can realistically recover the data.

Questions people ask

Why is my WD drive unreadable outside its case?

Many WD My Passport and My Book drives encrypt data using a key tied to the bridge board. A different adapter can leave the data unreadable.

Where is my BitLocker recovery key?

Often in your Microsoft account online, a work or school account, a printed page or a saved file.

Can someone crack it for me?

Not realistically. Strong encryption is designed to resist this, so be wary of anyone who says otherwise.

Before you start: Educational DIY guide, no warranty. DIY recovery can cause permanent data loss. If the data is valuable, consider a professional first.
